title: Learned quantum-battery controls link high stored energy with suppressed participation
summary: Soft actor-critic learning selected time-dependent couplings in a simulated anisotropic Dicke quantum battery with Kerr nonlinearity and photon loss. Compared with fixed couplings, the learned controls sustained higher stored energy alongside a persistently lower participation ratio. This is a conditional computed dynamical relationship, not a measured battery or proof of a general charging advantage.

source_review.scope: Primary v1 front, physical model, RL ResultsIII.3, conclusions and computational convergence context

evidence.tested: The learned policy changes rotating and counter-rotating couplings in the specified dissipative model. Participation-ratio trajectories were compared with a fixed-coupling reference across three Kerr strengths.
evidence.unknown: The result depends on the Hamiltonian, initial state, dissipative model and numerical truncation. Optimized variable controls have a broader control space than the fixed-coupling baseline. The participation ratio is a dynamical diagnostic, not an independently established universal mechanism. Separate analytically computed phase-transition results are not credited to AI; no physical device or energy-efficiency benefit was measured.
evidence.ai_role: A learned policy generates the time-dependent controls whose simulated energy and participation-ratio trajectories support the scoped dynamical finding.
